items.summary:
According to a New York Times report, Alice Huang maintained contact with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security for more than a year during her relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The reported period of communication spanned from spring 2025 until fall of the current year, based on intelligence reports described by sources cited in the article.

Huang previously led Megaspeed International, an Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in chip sales and has been under investigation since 2024 over concerns about smuggling advanced AI chips to China. The initial October 29 report suggesting Huang was a spy triggered Jensen Huang's resignation two weeks later and a decline in Nvidia's stock price.

US officials have cast doubt on the conclusion that Huang spied for China, with Attorney General Todd Blanche stating this month that the Justice Department had not reached a determination. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton echoed this position Sunday, noting the matter remains under investigation involving both Huang and her company.

The reporting has prompted broader questions from lawmakers about whether export controls on Chinese semiconductors have been enforced too loosely by the Trump administration.
items.title: NYT Report: Alice Huang Maintained Contact With Chinese Intelligence Officer During Affair

items.summary: In a blog post unveiled amid growing concern over the risks of rapidly advancing AI capabilities, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposed that developers adopt common limits on powerful models and use perplexity as an industry-standard metric for measuring progress. He described perplexity—a measure of how accurately a model predicts its next token—as an intelligence indicator in which lower values reflect better predictions. The proposal called for developers to commit not to exceed agreed capability thresholds until monitoring and safety mechanisms reach "a certain concrete milestone," with AI potentially driving fundamental training-method advances as early as 2027, possibly faster than progress in oversight and safety. Pachocki framed the plan around an industry standard defining a first development limit and specifying which milestones must be met before it is crossed. CEO Sam Altman endorsed the proposal on X, calling it "the most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile" and asserting that such limits would help ensure safety and control. The text presents these as proposals from Pachocki and Altman rather than established policy; no independent verification of their effectiveness or adoption is provided.
items.title: OpenAI Chief Scientist Proposes Industry-Wide AI Capability Limits Measured by Perplexity

items.summary: According to The New York Times, US President Donald Trump allegedly disregarded at least two intelligence warnings regarding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang, whom American officials regard as a suspected Chinese spy. Reports state that US intelligence agencies monitored Alice Huang's contact with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security between spring 2025 and autumn 2026, a period overlapping her alleged romance with Huang; the administration reportedly tracked these communications for over a year. National security advisers conveyed the findings to Trump on at least two occasions, but he is described as having dismissed them while continuing to defend Huang—whom officials say he considered an important ally and whose company Nvidia was viewed as vital to the economy—and even suggesting that Nvidia should reinstate him as chief executive in a November 21 statement. Trump publicly disputed the espionage allegations, stating on November 21 that 'I don't know that she is a spy' and implying that many beautiful women arriving from China are assumed to be spies; he also claimed no one had informed him of any intelligence identification of Alice Huang as a possible Chinese asset. The reporting extends beyond the personal relationship: Alice Huang's company Megaspeed reportedly acquired large quantities of advanced Nvidia chips, some allegedly routed through Southeast Asian data centres serving Chinese technology firms and possibly smuggled into China. Investigators are also examining her business partner Kang Wei, whom intelligence officials linked to China's Ministry of State Security; shipping records reportedly connect both individuals to companies involved in suspected chip smuggling. The investigation occurs against a backdrop of China's stated priority to overcome US technology restrictions for its artificial intelligence capabilities, with American authorities probing possible links between these activities and Chinese military programs. All claims are attributed as reports from The New York Times or officials' statements rather than confirmed fact; the article notes that Nvidia's board has rejected suggestions Huang return after his resignation earlier in the month over a separate workplace affair. Separately, the text includes biographical details about LiveMint journalist Sounak Mukhopadhyay, who authored coverage of the story.
items.title: Report: Trump reportedly dismissed intelligence warnings about Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang

items.summary: Microsoft is linking compensation in its Azure cloud division more closely to performance, announced via an internal memo from executive vice president Arun Ulagaratchagan. Top performers will receive additional stock awards while weaker results trigger formal manager meetings; the model also raises expectations for all employees by requiring them to close prior performance gaps and show a meaningful step-change in impact. The change was confirmed by Microsoft on Thursday, which stated that 'a world-class team like Azure requires world-class talent.' This pay overhaul follows an October 26 voluntary buyout offer extended to roughly 60,000 employees—more than a quarter of the company's reported 223,000-strong workforce—with level 70 and below staff in India included. The two moves target different groups: the buyouts aimed at departing employees while the pay model rewards those who stay with larger top-end incentives and closer scrutiny at the bottom; an employee-made pay spreadsheet reportedly already showed cloud and AI workers receiving the largest stock awards. CEO Satya Nadella framed both actions as part of a broader shift, noting that every Microsoft employee will eventually manage AI agents, citing Cowork in Microsoft 365 apps as built by just 11 developers.
items.title: Microsoft Ties Azure Pay to Performance Amid Workforce Buyouts and AI Spending

items.summary: During the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur's platinum jubilee celebrations, Google announced a grant described as approximately ₹46 crore (about $5 million) to advance AI research and education at the institute. The funding is directed toward three areas: applied AI research on real-world problems—specifically Indic languages, materials science, agriculture, and educational technology; training for students, faculty, teachers, and curriculum development; and capacity building through campus-based AI frameworks and tooling. Google CEO Sundar Pichai, an IIT Kharagpur alumnus, announced the partnership in a blog post, framing it as a way to accelerate work already underway at the institute while aligning with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of making AI benefits reach everyone in India. He expressed hope that the collaboration would shape future students similarly to how the institute shaped his own career.
items.title: Google's $5 Million Grant to IIT Kharagpur for AI Research and Education

items.summary: A Vice City-inspired aesthetic is trending on social media, with users transforming ordinary photos into colorful, cinematic character posters via AI image generators such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT. The process requires no professional editing skills; it involves uploading a high-resolution photo in which the face is clearly visible—ideally front-facing with good lighting—and avoiding heavy shadows, filters, or sunglasses to help the AI retain facial features. Users then enter detailed prompts specifying background, outfit, colors, lighting, and aesthetic, optionally asking the model to preserve their original face shape, hairstyle, and skin tone so the result stays recognizable. Follow-up instructions can adjust setting, clothing, pose, or lighting until desired. The article provides five example prompts: a GTA 6 character poster on a Vice City street with palm trees, pastel buildings, luxury cars, neon signs, and a dramatic sunset; a cinematic beach portrait at golden hour with ocean waves and pink-orange sky; a neon-lit night-time city portrait with glowing signboards, sports cars, and wet-road reflections in bold pink, purple, and blue lighting; a promotional poster posing beside a luxury car on a coastal road; and a tropical holiday look along a pastel street. All five prompts instruct the AI to omit text, logos, or watermarks.
items.title: How To Create GTA 6-Style AI Photos Using ChatGPT And Gemini To Share On Instagram: 5 Prompts To Try

items.summary: President Donald Trump publicly endorsed rehiring former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, posting on Truth Social that it would be 'the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.' The endorsement follows a New York Times report alleging that Alice Huang was in contact with an official of China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 through fall this year while reportedly engaging in a secret affair with Jensen Huang. According to the same reporting, US intelligence agencies have evidence suggesting her business partner, Kang Wei, also worked with the Chinese spy agency. National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton confirmed that investigations into Alice Huang and her company Megaspeed are ongoing alongside regulatory proceedings, and he stated his expectation that Nvidia's board would conduct a responsible review of the situation. Jensen Huang is expected to testify before three House Committees on December 1. However, both the Nvidia board and interim CEO Colette Kress have ruled out reinstating Huang at the top of leadership. The text notes as a caveat that Trump's endorsement may not be sufficient for Huang to secure a comeback given increasing pressure from Congress.
items.title: Trump Endorses Reinstating Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO Despite Board and Intelligence Findings

items.summary:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Hyderabad House in New Delhi for bilateral talks aimed at reviewing India-Nepal relations and expanding cooperation across key sectors. The discussions were scheduled to take place over two days (November 22-23), with the visit held at Modi's invitation, per the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). The agenda covered economic cooperation, trade, investment, transportation, infrastructure, energy, connectivity, as well as regional and international issues.

The MEA emphasized that bilateral relations are rooted in historical, cultural, and civilisational ties alongside strong people-to-people connections. Cooperation reportedly spans traditional sectors—trade and commerce, development partnership, energy, water resources, physical and digital connectivity—as well as newer areas including start-ups, technology, innovation, and sports.

Economic cooperation was expected to feature prominently, with both sides seeking to strengthen engagement in trade, transportation, investment, and infrastructure. The leaders were also anticipated to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management, and human resource development. Modi hosted an official luncheon for Shah and his 34-member delegation, which included Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor Kumar Byanjankar, and other senior officials.

Before the talks, Balen Shah paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat by laying a wreath and signing the visitors' book. The delegation had received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan in Modi's presence earlier that day.

items.title: India-Nepal Leaders Hold Bilateral Talks Focused on Trade, Energy, and Connectivity

items.summary: In response to safety findings against Bisleri's packaged drinking water, Indian authorities announced plans to conduct nationwide checks across packaged water brands. According to a government source cited by Reuters, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) initially declared a sample of Bisleri's product unsafe, prompting the regulator to sanction prosecution against both FSSAI and Bisleri International. A subsequent test reportedly found the samples compliant with safety standards. The proposed nationwide checks are intended as a follow-up measure following this controversy. Note that these plans were reported by a government source rather than confirmed details from official announcements.
items.title: India to Conduct Nationwide Packaged Water Safety Checks After Bisleri Controversy

items.summary:
A commentary by Amit John Kurien of RV University, Bengaluru argues that global studies on the drivers of deforestation inaccurately attribute forest loss to shifting cultivation (swidden farming), conflating land cover with land use and tree cover with forests. The author notes that estimating deforestation—defined as permanent conversion of forest to another land use—is only reliable when distinct land uses can be differentiated, yet influential mapping often coarsens spatial resolution by clustering land classes, trading accuracy for precision.

As supporting evidence, the commentary compares Philip Curtis et al.'s 2018 study (which ranked shifting agriculture as the second most important driver of global forest loss) with Andreas Heinimann et al.'s 2017 map of shifting cultivation. The authors found that approximately 4.5 million sq km—about 1.5 times the size of India—were misidentified globally as having shifting-agriculture-driven 'forest loss' despite no evidence in Heinimann's map, with two-thirds of this mismatch occurring in Africa.

The commentary attributes these errors partly to colonial-era framing that vilified shifting cultivation and led institutions like the FAO (1957) and post-colonial nations to stigmatize it; India's Wasteland Atlas classifies jhum as 'unproductive,' while Bangladesh and Myanmar use similar categories for land acquisition. The authors caution that misclassification has real-world consequences, enabling state or private takeover of communal upland lands used by millions of tribal farmers.

The commentary acknowledges these are the author's views drawn from published work with colleagues, and it does not provide quantitative estimates of actual shifting cultivation extent or forest loss—relying instead on map comparisons that identify mismatches rather than measuring true deforestation rates.
items.title: Why deforestation science gets shifting cultivation wrong

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced on Monday that it suspended the licenses of five nutraceutical and health supplement manufacturers—Vedant Remedies, Lucid Health Care Pvt Ltd, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare, Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals, and Adorreal Healthcare—for serious safety violations. Vedant Remedies was cited for poor hygiene, damaged infrastructure, lack of proper storage, expired food flavouring substances, and missing food safety records. Lucid Health Care's premises were found to have poor hygiene, inadequate lighting, improper storage, faulty pest control, and a failure to segregate Ayurvedic and nutraceutical products; handlers also lacked protective equipment and mandatory FoSTaC training, with food safety, testing, and maintenance records not properly maintained. Adorreal Healthcare's license was suspended because its licensed premises were non-operational due to ongoing construction while the company held an active FSSAI license against a disposed site and furnished false or misleading information; the suspension was issued under the Food Safety Act, 2006. Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals shifted from its licensed premises without endorsement of the new address on its existing license, and the relocated premises were shared with another food processing unit engaged in meat processing (M/s Myyo Foods India Private Limited). Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare's premises lacked hygiene, sanitation, and other compliance standards. The report was published on November 23, 2026.
items.title: FSSAI Suspends Licenses of Five Nutraceutical and Health Supplement Manufacturers Over Safety Violations

items.summary:
Chinese authorities announced that an official identified only by the surname Ma was sentenced to death for spying for a foreign intelligence service, with the penalty accompanied by a lifetime deprivation of political rights and forfeiture of all personal property. The case was publicized through a Monday post on WeChat's Baomiguan account, linked to the National Administration of State Secret Protection, as an admonition against leaking state secrets.

According to the post, Ma met a foreign intelligence officer named Kailin while stationed overseas and provided sensitive information including an internal telephone directory. He was later introduced to another officer, Tang Zheng, who threatened to report his prior illegal conduct unless he cooperated; Ma then agreed to supply confidential material using a dedicated laptop in exchange for more than 1 million yuan.

The announcement appears amid heightened attention to espionage involving China, following the March 2025 disclosure of a death sentence against former research institute employee Liu for espionage and illegally providing state secrets. The text also notes Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO this month after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The post did not name the foreign agency involved, disclose when the incident occurred, or reveal Ma's rank.
items.title: China Sentences Official to Death for Espionage

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has broadened its inspection of packaged drinking water brands after laboratory tests detected harmful substances in a sample from Bisleri International. Prosecution was initiated following these findings, while samples were also collected from numerous other manufacturers, including counterfeit brands; results for those remain pending.

Bisleri clarified that the contamination involved only a specific batch sourced from Goa and asserted its bottled water is safe overall. The company noted differences between packaged drinking water and mineral water in response to the notice.

The text presents these claims as reported statements rather than independently verified facts, with FSSAI emphasizing ongoing testing to ensure compliance with safety standards and protect public health. No specific details on the nature or concentration of harmful substances were provided.
items.title: FSSAI Expands Inspections of Packaged Drinking Water Brands After Bisleri Sample Found Unsafe

According to an exchange filing reported by Economic Times (written by Surbhi Khanna, who is not a SEBI-registered research analyst), Ashoka Buildcon secured two contracts from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the Jaipur Metro. The company's shares rose 7% following these announcements.

The first contract was for Rs 1,465 crore (excluding GST) to build an 8-lane, access-controlled stretch of the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway spanning 35.4 km from Jujuwa to Gandeva in Gujarat under EPC mode, with a defect liability period of 10 years and completion scheduled within 18 months.

The second contract was for Rs 1,628 crore to design and construct an elevated viaduct and 11 elevated stations as part of Jaipur Metro Phase-II MRTS Package 4 (Khasa Kothi/Phase-I), with a completion timeline of 36 months. items.summary: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay began replacing ceiling fan rods with wall-mounted fans in Hostel 4 on November 22, two months after a second-year student allegedly died by suicide there on September 18. The replacement was announced via an email from the general secretary for students' affairs and is intended to be extended to other hostels in phases over time. IIT Bombay framed the work as part of broader efforts to improve hostel safety and infrastructure, while also examining options such as student feedback surveys and consultations with representatives. Protesting students at the campus Justice Corner criticized the move, arguing that no scientific study establishes ceiling fan rods as a primary means of suicide and that the premise is illogical for a research institute to promote. The students called instead for structural accountability on academic pressure, caste- and gender-based discrimination, and inadequate channels for raising concerns, while urging the Student Council not to be co-opted into producing symbolic responses.
items.title: IIT Bombay Begins Replacing Ceiling Fan Rods After Student Suicide

items.summary:
The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Climate Change Convention, held in Antalya, Türkiye, concluded on Sunday without reaching consensus on its cover decision. India's Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav confirmed that no pact was adopted because the European Union and other nations disagreed with oil-dependent economies such as Saudi Arabia over phasing out fossil fuels. The conference ran two days past its scheduled Friday end date.

The EU, backed by more than 130 countries (per AFP), insisted any agreement include a provision to phase out fossil fuels; Panama, Vanuatu, and the Marshall Islands joined this stance. Oil-producing states opposed including such language in the final deal. Because UN decisions require consensus, opposition from even one country is sufficient to block an agreement.

At COP30 in Brazil last year, the EU and more than 80 other countries had called for a fossil fuel phase-out roadmap but withdrew that demand after oil-dependent economies gained support from major powers including India and China. Those nations advocated instead for a phase-down—reducing rather than eliminating fossil fuels entirely—citing economic dependence on coal and petrol.

After the talks, Yadav said India remained committed to dialogue while raising concerns about historical emissions consuming a disproportionate share of the global carbon budget and calling for equity and climate justice. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed disappointment at the lack of consensus, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attributed the failure to difficult geopolitical times.

The last similar outcome occurred at COP15 in Copenhagen (2009), where negotiations aimed at a new agreement were not finalized until six years later in Paris.
items.title: COP31 Ends Without Agreement Over Fossil Fuel Phase-Out

items.summary: Seat-sharing negotiations between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress for Uttar Pradesh's 2027 Assembly elections formally began in Delhi on Monday with a brief first-round meeting between four-member panels from each party. The talks, described as taking place in a 'cordial atmosphere,' focused on finalizing an agenda and seat-allocation approach across the state's 403 Assembly constituencies. SP panel head Ram Gopal Yadav stated that both parties listened to one another's points of view and would complete the process within two to three days, with further meetings scheduled for subsequent days. Congress representatives echoed this positive tone: UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said an agreement is 'nearly settled,' while Aradhana Misra (Mona) expressed confidence that finalization could occur within two to four days and emphasized that the formula would be based on winnability rather than rigid numbers. Congress MP Pramod Tiwari noted both sides were examining constituency-wise strengths and data, with additional meetings possible if required. The SP panel comprises Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyam Lal Pal, Ghosi Lok Sabha MP Rajiv Rai, and Kairana Lok Sabha MP Iqra Chaudhary (Iqra Hasan). The Congress panel includes UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra (Mona), state working president Imran Masood, and AICC general secretary KC Venugopal. These structured panels mark a formal start to opposition coordination within the INDIA bloc ahead of 2027. The Congress had earlier indicated interest in contesting around 181 constituencies, while the SP maintained that allocation must rest on local strength, past performance, and realistic winning prospects—reflecting the party's dominance after it won 111 seats versus two for Congress in the 2022 Assembly elections. The first phase (November 23–24) would examine constituencies individually to avoid vote division against the BJP while maximizing overall tally.
items.title: Samajwadi Party and Congress Begin Formal UP Seat-Sharing Talks for 2027 Elections

items.summary: In the domestic market, MCX silver futures for December 2026 delivery rose Rs 3,600 (2.5%) to Rs 1,51,390 per kg after a 4-day fall, while gold futures for the same month climbed Rs 2,800 (2.3%) to Rs 1,24,550 per 10 grams, snapping a 5-day losing streak. The price movements occurred against a backdrop of ongoing speculation about US Federal Reserve monetary policy: Fed Governor Lisa Cook argued on Friday that the current rate was insufficient to address inflation she described with "great concern," while ECB member Alvaro Santos Pereira noted persistent energy-related inflation pressures from rising natural gas prices, though their spread across the euro zone remained unclear. Markets were pricing a 93% probability of an interest rate hike at the Fed's December meeting per CME's FedWatch tool; higher rates generally raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like gold and silver, making them less attractive to investors. On international markets, spot gold rose 1.2% to $3,576.10 per ounce by 0048 GMT after recovering from Friday's decline—its lowest since September 2025—and following a roughly 9% weekly drop, its steepest since March; spot silver gained 2.3% to $42.11, platinum advanced 1.4% to $1,316.97, and palladium climbed 1.3% to $904.15. Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart (an SEBI-registered research analyst) characterized gold and silver as deeply oversold, suggesting any positive Fed signals could trigger a sharp recovery while warning of continued volatility driven by crude oil prices, the dollar index, and rate-hike concerns; he set technical support/resistance levels for both metals on international and MCX markets. He advised long-term investors to accumulate via SIPs during the correction but cautioned traders against fresh long positions until stability returns. Physical gold rates in Indian cities ranged from Rs 91,712/8 grams (standard) to Rs 1,00,176/8 grams (pure), with Delhi slightly higher than Mumbai, Chennai, and Hyderabad. The article's price movements are reported facts, but the trading recommendations reflect only Jain's individual views as an analyst; readers were advised that these should not be construed as ETMarkets' own guidance.
items.title: MCX Gold and Silver Prices Rise After Recent Declines Amid Fed Rate-Hike Speculation

items.summary: A 17-year-old girl in Kerala's Areekode police jurisdiction alleged that using a fairness cream marketed as 'F Tune' caused serious health complications, including kidney damage. The teenager reportedly discovered the product through Instagram advertisements promising to clear pimples and pigmentation while giving skin a glowing appearance; she ordered it via WhatsApp and used it for nearly a year before developing what doctors at Aster MIMS Mother Hospital described as a serious kidney condition requiring treatment costing about Rs 1 lakh (approximately $12,000). Laboratory tests cited by the treating physicians detected mercury levels of 12,500 parts per million in the cream, far exceeding the permissible limit of less than 1 ppm. The complaint alleges that the producer knew of the health risks associated with excessive mercury yet continued selling it. Police registered a case under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, and the Kerala Police Act after the teenager's complaint from Ugrapuram, naming the cream's producer as an accused while further investigation continues.
items.title: Kerala teen alleges kidney damage from mercury-laced fairness cream as state launches crackdown on fake cosmetics

items.summary: Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi questioned the testing methodology used by the Karnataka government to detect ethanol content in petrol, dismissing concerns over fuel with higher-than-prescribed ethanol levels. In response to reports that tests found 27% and 28% ethanol—exceeding prescribed standards—Gopi called these reported figures 'unacceptable' and raised doubts about whether samples were collected directly from refineries rather than at retail outlets. He argued that fuel passes through multiple stages, including transportation and storage in underground tanks at retail points, which are not currently monitored or sealed by the government. Gopi maintained that oil companies bear responsibility for complying with Union regulations and that periodic checks ensure adherence to standards, while insisting the issue should not be politicized. Defending E20 fuel more broadly, he cited Paraguay and Brazil as examples of higher blending levels and stated India's blending percentage could rise to 30% or 40% in future, contingent on scientific assessments and regulatory requirements. He also rejected claims that consumers are being compelled to use E20 petrol, asserting people retain the choice not to purchase it. The minister acknowledged Kerala's right to conduct its own tests but indicated central authorities would submit their own reports for legal resolution.
items.title: Suresh Gopi Questions Karnataka's E20 Testing and Defends Ethanol Blending

items.summary:
A global sell-off in gold—driven primarily by forced liquidation of debt-heavy, overvalued AI stocks (US tech logged its worst session since COVID the same week Anthropic raised $81.3 billion on a 17 per cent surge) and fears of central-bank rate hikes—drove international prices down nearly 10 per cent in one week from January's record of $5,594.82 per ounce (about $180 per gram). While Asian markets saw sharp cuts, physical demand surged in India and China; silver fell over 60 per cent from its January peak while gold dropped more than 30 per cent globally. The correction is playing out unevenly across India: mutual-fund and ETF investors face large unrealized losses, exchange traders hit by margin calls, but wedding-season jewellery buyers benefit from cheaper prices amid a boom in showroom activity.

The article disputes Prime Minister Narendra Modi's claim that his earlier appeal to avoid non-essential gold purchases caused the domestic price correction. It notes international prices fell over 30 per cent from January's record versus Modi comparing only one day before his announcement, and that the reversal began in January 2026—before any government exhortation. In May, import duties on gold and silver were more than doubled (from 6 per cent to 15 per cent) partly to curb imports and support the rupee. World Gold Council data show India's market is a volume-and-value story: demand fell 12 per cent to 444 tonnes in nine months, yet value rose 38 per cent to Rs.6,688 billion ($71 billion), because high prices limited quantities but not total spending.

The most pressing risk stems from gold-financing NBFCs—Muthoot Finance, IIFL Finance, Bajaj Finance, and Manappuram Finance—which reported increased stage 2 assets (early stress or delinquency) as defaults loom for both lenders and their customers. The piece concludes that while the short term may offer some buyers a window of opportunity, prolonged price damage threatens Indian households already burdened by loans and rising costs; it likens Modi's self-attribution to "fool's gold," cautioning readers to distinguish real accomplishments from bogus claims.
items.title: Gold's Global Sell-Off Overshadowed by AI Volatility and Debunking of Modi Credit

items.summary: Following the International Court of Justice verdict on November 19 finding Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya, Noorul Amin—a 26-year-old Rohingya refugee who arrived in India at age eight—expressed hope that the ruling would lead to more humane treatment for refugees living in India. The ICJ found that Myanmar's military operations in Rakhine State killed an estimated 10,000 Rohingya and prompted at least seven lakh (700,000) of them to flee to Bangladesh; it also noted decades of discriminatory measures that eroded the group's political and civil rights. Amin arrived via a makeshift boat built from bamboo in 2007 after his family fled what he described as a bloodbath, while his wife Zahida crossed into India on foot in 2020 at nearly age 18; both families had faced persecution since the early 2010s. Despite holding UN refugee cards—which have been issued by the UN since 2011—Amin's family experienced repeated detentions, including a five-month detention for him and his wife in Madanpur Khader after their arrest in 2020, while his parents spent three years detained. In May 2025, amid an Indian crackdown on 'Bangladeshi migrants' following the Pahalgam terror attack, Amin's family was among roughly 40 Rohingya flown to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands before being forced off a navy vessel into the sea toward Myanmar; his parents were never returned. India is not a signatory to UN refugee law or protocols and maintains that existing foreigner laws suffice. On economic grounds, Amin reported struggling to earn enough for rent of Rs 5,000–6,000 per month, sometimes skipping meals. Sabber Kyaw Min of the Rohingya Human Rights Initiative cited an estimated 22,000 Rohingya refugees in India as of latest figures. Amin's family had secured U.S. visas through UN resettlement but were blocked after Donald Trump took office in January 2025 and imposed travel restrictions; he also noted that Indian courts dismissed petitions against the deportations, with one bench calling it a 'beautifully crafted story.' The account reflects one refugee's perspective on India's policies and does not represent verified official statistics or comprehensive coverage of all Rohingya experiences.
items.title: Rohingya Refugee Hopes ICJ Genocide Verdict Will Improve India's Treatment of Refugees
